title: Amos 4 — The cows of Bashan, the refrain of the plagues, and he who forms the mountains

verdicts.reasoning: pārôṯ habbāšān ... hāʾōməroṯ laʾăḏōnêhem hāḇîʾâ wəništeh: 'their lords' keeps ʾăḏōnîm (ASV) with NRSV 'husbands' in commentary; the masculine suffix is reported. Exact.

nišbaʿ ʾăḏōnāy YHWH bəqoḏšô ... wənissāʾ ʾeṯḵem bəṣinnôṯ wəʾaḥărîṯḵen bəsîrôṯ dûḡâ: 'the Lord YHWH' (central adonai-yhwh) and the ASV 'hooks ... fish-hooks' are kept, with the container reading in commentary. Exact.

citations: Andersen and Freedman, Amos (AB 24A, 1989), ad loc.

Non-blocking: the note attributes 'the dung-heap' to Aquila; the reviewer could not confirm that attribution. Verify it or cite the reading as a modern emendation via Andersen and Freedman or Paul.
bōʾû ḇêṯ-ʾēl ûp̄išʿû ... lišlōšeṯ yāmîm maʿśərōṯêḵem: ASV, exact; the priestly-summons parody is correctly described.
wəqaṭṭēr mēḥāmēṣ tôḏâ wəqirʾû nəḏāḇôṯ hašmîʿû ... nəʾum ʾăḏōnāy YHWH: the infinitive absolute is rendered as an imperative in sequence, following the ASV. Exact.
niqyôn šinnayim ... wəḥōser leḥem ... wəlōʾ-šaḇtem ʿāḏay nəʾum-YHWH: exact; refrain consistent across vv6-11.
The rain withheld bəʿôḏ šəlōšâ ḥŏḏāšîm laqqāṣîr and the city-by-city alternation are rendered closely. Exact.
wənāʿû štayim šālōš ʿārîm ... wəlōʾ yiśbāʿû: 'wandered' for nûaʿ (staggered) is the ASV word. Exact.
hikkêṯî ʾeṯḵem baššiddāp̄ôn ûḇayyērāqôn harbôṯ gannôṯêḵem ... yōʾḵal haggāzām: the MT infinitive is kept and NRSV's emendation reported, per the textual policy. Exact.
šillaḥtî ḇāḵem deḇer bəḏereḵ miṣrayim ... ʿim šəḇî sûsêḵem ... bəʾōš maḥănêḵem ûḇəʾappəḵem: 'captured horses' is literal and 'even into your nostrils' renders the waw. Exact.

citations: Wolff, Joel and Amos (Hermeneia, 1977), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: hāp̄aḵtî ḇāḵem kəmahpēḵaṯ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-səḏōm ...: 'as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah' matches isaiah-woh 13:19 for the same formula. The superlative reading is reported. Line approved; 'God' depends on F1.

citations: Wolff, Joel and Amos (Hermeneia, 1977), ad loc.

citations: Andersen and Freedman, Amos (AB 24A, 1989), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: Disputed against the corpus 'shape' only: ûḇōrēʾ rûaḥ is rendered 'creates the wind', as in ASV ('createth'), NRSV and NJPS and in the isaiah-woh bara-create ruling; the object is not a material. bāmŏṯê ʾāreṣ 'the high places of the earth' is the standard theophanic idiom (Mic 1:3), and śēḥô is kept with the LXX christon reported. The reception note matches TBWTT ch. 3 ('He ... that treadeth upon the high places of the earth') and is labelled; the line carries no lens.

glossaryReview.reasoning: direct is right for a presentation convention with no interpretive content. Verified in the lines: English names, 'the Lord YHWH' / 'the Lord', unquoted messenger formula (Jer 10:2, 18), quoted speech inside oracles and visions, and nəʾum 'declares' kept distinct from ʾāmar 'says' (Zech 4:6 against 5:4). Two open points are recorded under founder recommendations: F3, where the reviewer supports 'declares', and F4, where the reviewer supports ratification. The versional readings listed are reported and not adopted, and the rafe at Zech 5:11 is handled correctly. direct is right for a textual policy consistent with the corpus.

reviewerReport.lensLeakageCheck: Checked all 13 lines in the English alone. No English line reads as interpretation. The canon-cited verses (4:13) render the Hebrew at standard values, and each reception note is under its own 'Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim)' heading. Each note's quotation was verified against the canon text (TBWTT ch. 3 and ch. 5, FR/EN). Capitalisation (e.g. 'the Fish Gate') and vocabulary updates ('scroll', 'lampstand') are register or name conventions with lexical basis, not lens.
reviewerReport.escalationReportAdjustments: Initial verdicts on all 109 LP1 lines, 31 overlay entries and 27 central ops were formed from the chapters, the sources, the drafts, the overlays and the diff, and recorded before wave-lp1-editor-report.md was opened. After reading it, no verdict changed. The report's watch points were each re-tested: Zeph 1:18 'earth', Zeph 1:10-11 names, Zech 4:14, Zech 9:9, Jer 10:5 and the unquoted Jer 10:2-5. The report does not mention the two Zech 4 speech-line issues (4:10 quote boundary; 4:13 'answered'), which stand as revise. The founder points F1-F5 are answered below.

founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-isaiah-aligned-conventions: Ratify for the Latter Prophets: 'God', 'earth'/'land' by scope, lowercase 'spirit', 'create' and 'oracle' are each the ASV/NRSV/NJPS-backed rendering and keep the five books one volume with Isaiah. Harmonize Ezekiel at its next wave, not by retro-editing signed-off chapters. The 'God'/'Elohim' split is the one item the reviewer flags for explicit founder ratification, because it is a project-stance choice.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F2-officials-shofar-vs-isaiah: Align Isaiah to 'officials' (Isa 32:1; 40:23; 43:28) and 'shofar' (Isa 27:13) at its next pass; both are lexically better grounded and already corpus rulings. Then promote megillah/menorah/sarim/shofar to central entries as the report proposes. Keep the Exodus 25 'lampstand' dependency on the Exodus checklist.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F3-neum-declares: Adopt 'declares YHWH' corpus-wide. Zechariah has ʾāmar YHWH (4:6) and nəʾum YHWH (5:4) within a few verses, and Isaiah's 'says' for both (e.g. ISA-14:22, checked) erases a distinction the Hebrew makes. Align Isaiah later.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-unquoted-messenger-formula: Ratify. At Jer 10:2-6 the Hebrew does not mark where the oracle ends, and leaving it unquoted avoids inventing a boundary. Related: at Zech 4:9-10 the wave's own marks run YHWH's word into the messenger's answer, which is the reviewer's revise at ZEC-WOH-4:10.
founderDecisionRecommendations.F5-sons-of-fresh-oil: Ship 'the two sons of fresh oil'. It is the most literal rendering, lexically grounded (yiṣhār, no māšaḥ), and inferred is the honest label; 'anointed ones' stays in commentary for reception continuity. If the founder wants a gentler line, 'the two sons of oil' (ASV margin) is the conservative literal fallback.

paragraphs.text: שִׁמְע֞וּ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה פָּר֤וֹת הַבָּשָׁן֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּהַ֣ר שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן הָעֹשְׁק֣וֹת דַּלִּ֔ים הָרֹצְצ֖וֹת אֶבְיוֹנִ֑ים הָאֹמְרֹ֥ת לַאֲדֹֽנֵיהֶ֖ם הָבִ֥יאָה וְנִשְׁתֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to their lords, "Bring, that we may drink!"

notes.official: *pārôṯ habbāšān* 'cows of Bashan': the wealthy women of Samaria, named after the cattle of the richest pasture-land (Deut 32:14; Ps 22:13). *laʾăḏōnêhem* 'to their lords' has a masculine suffix for the feminine 'cows', one of several gender mismatches in this oracle (cf. v2). *ʾăḏōnîm* is kept as 'lords' (ASV); NRSV's 'husbands' is an interpretation (overlay `lexical-cruxes-amos-4`; Paul, *Amos*, Hermeneia, 1991). Their words 'Bring, that we may drink!' are speech quoted inside the oracle and keep their marks (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: נִשְׁבַּ֨ע אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ בְּקָדְשׁ֔וֹ כִּ֛י הִנֵּ֥ה יָמִ֖ים בָּאִ֣ים עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְנִשָּׂ֤א אֶתְכֶם֙ בְּצִנּ֔וֹת וְאַחֲרִיתְכֶ֖ן בְּסִיר֥וֹת דּוּגָֽה׃

i18n.en: The Lord YHWH has sworn by his holiness that, behold, days are coming upon you when they shall take you away with hooks, and the last of you with fish-hooks.

notes.official: *nišbaʿ ʾăḏōnāy YHWH bəqoḏšô* 'The Lord YHWH has sworn by his holiness' (central `adonai-yhwh`; cf. 6:8; 8:7). *wənissāʾ ʾeṯḵem* 'they shall take you away', literally 'one will lift you'. *ṣinnôṯ* and *sîrôṯ dûḡâ* are uncertain: 'hooks ... fish-hooks' (ASV, NRSV), or containers, 'baskets ... fish-pots' (Paul, Hermeneia). Either way the deportees are carried off like a catch. The line keeps the ASV (overlay `lexical-cruxes-amos-4`).

paragraphs.text: וּפְרָצִ֥ים תֵּצֶ֖אנָה אִשָּׁ֣ה נֶגְדָּ֑הּ וְהִשְׁלַכְתֶּ֥נָה הַהַרְמ֖וֹנָה נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And you shall go out at the breaches, every woman straight before her, and you shall cast yourselves into Harmon, declares YHWH.

notes.official: *ûp̄ərāṣîm tēṣeʾnâ* 'you shall go out at the breaches' in the city wall, each woman straight ahead. *wəhišlaḵtenâ hahharmônâ*: the Hiphil has no object, and *harmôn* is unknown. The line keeps the ASV's 'you shall cast yourselves into Harmon', transliterating the place-name; proposals include Mount Hermon (NRSV, emending), 'the dung-heap' (by comparison with *madmēnâ*) and the Old Greek's 'the mountain Romman' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-amos-4`; Andersen and Freedman, *Amos*, AB 24A, 1989). *nəʾum-YHWH* 'declares YHWH' (`house-conventions-latter-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: בֹּ֤אוּ בֵֽית־אֵל֙ וּפִשְׁע֔וּ הַגִּלְגָּ֖ל הַרְבּ֣וּ לִפְשֹׁ֑עַ וְהָבִ֤יאוּ לַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ זִבְחֵיכֶ֔ם לִשְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת יָמִ֖ים מַעְשְׂרֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: Come to Bethel and transgress; to Gilgal, and multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days;

notes.official: An ironic call to worship in the form of a priestly summons: 'Come to Bethel and transgress' parodies 'Come to Bethel and worship'. *zeḇaḥ* 'sacrifice' (central `qorbanot-sacrificial-offering-vocabulary-cluster-cross-corpus`); *maʿśərōṯêḵem* 'your tithes'. *lišlōšeṯ yāmîm* 'every three days' (ASV; NJPS 'on the third day') matches the hyperbole of 'every morning' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-amos-4`).

paragraphs.text: וְקַטֵּ֤ר מֵֽחָמֵץ֙ תּוֹדָ֔ה וְקִרְא֥וּ נְדָב֖וֹת הַשְׁמִ֑יעוּ כִּ֣י כֵ֤ן אֲהַבְתֶּם֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃

i18n.en: and offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving of that which is leavened, and proclaim freewill-offerings, publish them; for so you love to do, children of Israel, declares the Lord YHWH.

notes.official: *qaṭṭēr mēḥāmēṣ tôḏâ* 'offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving of that which is leavened': leaven was forbidden on the altar (Lev 2:11), though leavened bread accompanied the thank-offering (Lev 7:13). The irony is aimed at zeal without obedience. *nəḏāḇôṯ* 'freewill-offerings' (ASV). *nəʾum ʾăḏōnāy YHWH* 'declares the Lord YHWH' (central `adonai-yhwh`).

paragraphs.text: וְגַם־אֲנִי֩ נָתַ֨תִּי לָכֶ֜ם נִקְי֤וֹן שִׁנַּ֙יִם֙ בְּכָל־עָ֣רֵיכֶ֔ם וְחֹ֣סֶר לֶ֔חֶם בְּכֹ֖ל מְקוֹמֹֽתֵיכֶ֑ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: And I also gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places; yet you have not returned to me, declares YHWH.

notes.official: The first of five strophes (vv6-11), each closing with the refrain *wəlōʾ-šaḇtem ʿāḏay nəʾum-YHWH* 'yet you have not returned to me, declares YHWH'. The plagues follow the covenant curses of Lev 26 and Deut 28. *niqyôn šinnayim* 'cleanness of teeth' is famine (ASV).

paragraphs.text: וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִי֩ מָנַ֨עְתִּי מִכֶּ֜ם אֶת־הַגֶּ֗שֶׁם בְּע֨וֹד שְׁלֹשָׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ לַקָּצִ֔יר וְהִמְטַרְתִּי֙ עַל־עִ֣יר אֶחָ֔ת וְעַל־עִ֥יר אַחַ֖ת לֹ֣א אַמְטִ֑יר חֶלְקָ֤ה אַחַת֙ תִּמָּטֵ֔ר וְחֶלְקָ֛ה אֲשֶֽׁר־לֹֽא־תַמְטִ֥יר עָלֶ֖יהָ תִּיבָֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: And I also withheld the rain from you when there were yet three months to the harvest; and I caused it to rain on one city, and caused it not to rain on another city; one piece was rained on, and the piece on which it did not rain withered.

notes.official: The rain withheld 'three months to the harvest' is the late spring rain on which the grain harvest depends. *ḥelqâ* 'piece' of ground (ASV).

paragraphs.text: וְנָע֡וּ שְׁתַּיִם֩ שָׁלֹ֨שׁ עָרִ֜ים אֶל־עִ֥יר אַחַ֛ת לִשְׁתּ֥וֹת מַ֖יִם וְלֹ֣א יִשְׂבָּ֑עוּ וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: So two or three cities wandered to one city to drink water, and were not satisfied; yet you have not returned to me, declares YHWH.

paragraphs.text: הִכֵּ֣יתִי אֶתְכֶם֮ בַּשִּׁדָּפ֣וֹן וּבַיֵּרָקוֹן֒ הַרְבּ֨וֹת גַּנּוֹתֵיכֶ֧ם וְכַרְמֵיכֶ֛ם וּתְאֵנֵיכֶ֥ם וְזֵיתֵיכֶ֖ם יֹאכַ֣ל הַגָּזָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: I struck you with blight and with mildew; the multitude of your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees the locust devoured; yet you have not returned to me, declares YHWH.

notes.official: *šiddāp̄ôn* and *yērāqôn* 'blight and mildew' (ASV) are the pair of Deut 28:22 and 1 Kgs 8:37. *harbôṯ gannôṯêḵem* 'the multitude of your gardens' is the MT infinitive (ASV); NRSV emends to *heḥĕraḇtî* 'I laid waste your gardens', and the MT is kept (overlay `lexical-cruxes-amos-4`; `mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`). *kerem* 'vineyard' (central `kerem-vineyard`). *gāzām* 'the locust' (ASV 'the palmer-worm').

paragraphs.text: שִׁלַּ֨חְתִּי בָכֶ֥ם דֶּ֙בֶר֙ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם הָרַ֤גְתִּי בַחֶ֙רֶב֙ בַּח֣וּרֵיכֶ֔ם עִ֖ם שְׁבִ֣י סֽוּסֵיכֶ֑ם וָאַעֲלֶ֞ה בְּאֹ֤שׁ מַחֲנֵיכֶם֙ וּֽבְאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

i18n.en: I sent among you a pestilence after the manner of Egypt; I slew your young men with the sword, together with your captured horses; and I made the stench of your camps come up even into your nostrils; yet you have not returned to me, declares YHWH.

notes.official: *bəḏereḵ miṣrayim* 'after the manner of Egypt' recalls the plagues of the Exodus (Ex 9:3; Deut 28:27, 60). *ʿim šəḇî sûsêḵem* 'together with your captured horses' is literal (ASV 'and have carried away your horses'). *wāʾaʿăleh bəʾōš maḥănêḵem ûḇəʾappəḵem* 'I made the stench of your camps come up even into your nostrils' (overlay `lexical-cruxes-amos-4`).

paragraphs.text: הָפַ֣כְתִּי בָכֶ֗ם כְּמַהְפֵּכַ֤ת אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־סְדֹ֣ם וְאֶת־עֲמֹרָ֔ה וַתִּהְי֕וּ כְּא֖וּד מֻצָּ֣ל מִשְׂרֵפָ֑ה וְלֹֽא־שַׁבְתֶּ֥ם עָדַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: I overthrew some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a brand plucked out of the burning; yet you have not returned to me, declares YHWH.

notes.official: *kəmahpēḵaṯ ʾĕlōhîm ʾeṯ-səḏōm wəʾeṯ-ʿămōrâ* 'as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah' is the fixed Sodom formula (Deut 29:22; Isa 13:19; Jer 49:18; 50:40), rendered with the *hpk* lexeme kept (central `mahapekhah-overthrowing-formula`). *ʾĕlōhîm* is rendered 'God' (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`), as isaiah-woh renders the same formula at 13:19; the draft's 'Elohim' followed the Genesis-scoped central entry. YHWH speaks of God in the third person because the formula is quoted whole; some read *ʾĕlōhîm* as a superlative, 'a mighty overthrow'. *kəʾûḏ muṣṣāl miśśərēp̄â* 'like a brand plucked out of the burning' (cf. Zech 3:2).

paragraphs.text: לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אֶעֱשֶׂה־לְּךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֵ֚קֶב כִּֽי־זֹ֣את אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ הִכּ֥וֹן לִקְרַאת־אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Therefore thus will I do to you, Israel; because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel.

notes.official: *lāḵēn kōh ʾeʿĕśeh-ləḵā* 'Therefore thus will I do to you': the threat is left unstated, which makes it more ominous (Wolff, *Joel and Amos*, Hermeneia, 1977). *hikkôn liqraʾṯ-ʾĕlōhêḵā* 'prepare to meet your God' (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`) uses the language of the Sinai theophany (Ex 19:11, 15, 17).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֡י הִנֵּה֩ יוֹצֵ֨ר הָרִ֜ים וּבֹרֵ֣א ר֗וּחַ וּמַגִּ֤יד לְאָדָם֙ מַה־שֵּׂח֔וֹ עֹשֵׂ֥ה שַׁ֙חַר֙ עֵיפָ֔ה וְדֹרֵ֖ךְ עַל־בָּ֣מֳתֵי אָ֑רֶץ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: For behold, he who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what his thought is; who makes the morning darkness, and treads on the high places of the earth — YHWH, the God of hosts, is his name.

notes.official:
A hymnic doxology, the first of three in Amos (4:13; 5:8-9; 9:5-6), each ending with the name formula (overlay `bamote-aretz-theophany-hymn-amos-4-13`). *yôṣēr hārîm* 'he who forms the mountains' (central `yatsar`). *ûḇōrēʾ rûaḥ* 'and creates the wind': *bārāʾ* is rendered 'create' (`bara-create-latter-prophets`, as isaiah-woh), replacing the draft's 'shapes', which applied the Genesis-scoped central *bara*; *rûaḥ* is the physical wind set beside the mountains (`ruach-spirit-wind-breath-latter-prophets`). *ûmaggîḏ ləʾāḏām mah-śēḥô* 'and declares to man what his thought is': *śēaḥ* is a hapax, and 'his' may be man's own thought or God's purpose (cf. 3:7); the Old Greek read *māšîḥô* 'his anointed' (*christon autou*), and the MT is kept (`mt-qere-textual-policy-latter-prophets`). *ʿōśēh šaḥar ʿêp̄â* 'who makes the morning darkness' (ASV; central `asah`; the Old Greek and NJPS have 'dawn and darkness'). *wəḏōrēḵ ʿal-bāmŏṯê ʾāreṣ* 'and treads on the high places of the earth': *bāmâ* is here the topographic height, not the cultic 'high place', and the clause is the image of the divine warrior striding over the earth (Mic 1:3; Deut 32:13; Job 9:8). *ʾereṣ* is the earth in this cosmic hymn (`eretz-earth-or-land-latter-prophets`; ASV, NRSV, NJPS), replacing the draft's 'the land'. *YHWH ʾĕlōhê-ṣəḇāʾôṯ šəmô* 'YHWH, the God of hosts, is his name' (`elohim-god-latter-prophets`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 3) quotes the clause '... He ... that treadeth upon the high places of the earth' and reads it as the trace of the creators' bases on the high mountains. The line renders *bāmŏṯê ʾāreṣ* by the standard 'the high places of the earth' and gives the clause no sense beyond the Hebrew theophanic idiom.
